76	12. **Always run `flow format` after edits** — `uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow` is the canonical layout step. 119	
120	## Anti-patterns
121	
122	<!--skill-flavor:project-creation-antipatterns:start-->
123	- **Prefer running `uip maestro flow init` from inside the solution you named** — run outside one it auto-scaffolds `<Project>Solution/`, but the auto name won't match your chosen solution name. Never pass `--skip-solution-registration` for a project you intend to upload (it leaves a bare single-nested layout). See [SKILL.md rule #6](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) for the required double-nested `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` layout and the self-check.
124	<!--skill-flavor:project-creation-antipatterns:end-->
125	- **Never guess node schemas** — use `registry get` for all node types. Guessed port names or input fields cause silent wiring failures.
126	- **Never guess the value or format of a business output** — when a request names an output (`caseKey`, `ticketId`, `severity`, …) without saying how to derive it, elicit the rule ([SKILL.md rule #5](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal)) or confirm your assumption before building. Inventing a format — e.g. prefixing an id that should pass through unchanged — yields a flow that passes `flow validate` but returns the wrong business outcome at runtime. See rule #17 above.
127	- **Never skip capability discovery for connector nodes** — run `registry search` to confirm the connector exists and what operations it supports before building. See [connector/planning.md](references/plugins/connector/planning.md). Skipping this is the #1 cause of designing around a connector that doesn't exist or an operation it doesn't support.
128	- **Never replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run** — if `registry search` / `registry get` finds `uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<operation>`, add that real connector node via `uip maestro flow node add`. Missing live connections, missing tenant access, or prompts that ask you to only plan `--detail` mean: run `node add`, write the planned `--detail` payload to a sidecar file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`), and surface "configure pending" as an Open Question. **Do not leave a partial `inputs.detail` on the node** — the validator rejects hand-authored envelopes, and the node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run. Studio Web and reviewers need the real connector key in the `.flow`; the agent must report this explicitly rather than letting the user discover it via a later validation failure. See [§ Node ownership](#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) and [connector/impl.md — No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration](references/plugins/connector/impl.md#no-live-tenant--planned-configuration).
129	- **Never set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on a node with no outgoing `error` edge** — the flag is CLI-owned (`edge add --source-port error` and `flow format` derive it from the error edges actually present). A hand-set flag with no handler suppresses the node's fault, so the failure is swallowed and the run reports success. See rule #16 above.
130	- **Never route an `error` port back into the happy path** — an error edge into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failed run report `Completed` with success-shaped outputs. Send it to a distinct End node with an error/status output, to `core.logic.terminate`, or to a branch that genuinely recovers.
131	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
132	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
133	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
134	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
135	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
136	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
137	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
138	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
139	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
140	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
141	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
142	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
143	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
144	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
145	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
146	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
147	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker. Strip it and pass a `=js:` expression returning the array (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": "=js:(['a', 'b'])"`). Never a literal JSON array — it validates but does not bind. 1	# HITL Node — Planning
2	
3	The flow needs to pause for a human to review, approve, or fill in data. Two node types serve this need — choose based on form complexity and whether an app already exists.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Which HITL Node to Use
8	
9	| Use case | Node type | Form source |
10	| --- | --- | --- |
11	| Inline form designed right now (fields + outcomes defined in the flow) | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` | Schema embedded in node inputs — no app needed |
12	| Existing coded app or Action Center app | `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app` | Deployed app from Orchestrator |
13	
14	**Prefer `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`** for new flows. It is an OOTB node — no registry discovery, no app publishing, no tenant dependency.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
19	
20	Node type: `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`
21	Available: always — no `uip login` or registry pull required.
22	
23	### When to Select
24	
25	| Situation | Select? |
26	| --- | --- |
27	| Manager approval before processing | Yes |
28	| Human reviews extracted data before submission | Yes |
29	| Human resolves exceptions the automation cannot handle | Yes |
30	| Need a quick form with specific fields and outcomes | Yes |
31	| Existing coded/Action Center app should be used | No — use Option 2 |
32	| Fully automated processing, no human involvement | No |
33	
34	### Ports
35	
36	| Input port | Output port |
37	| --- | --- |
38	| `input` | `outcome-completed` |
39	
40	**The output port must be wired.** A node with no edge on `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely.
41	
42	### Output Variables
43	
44	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object containing all output and inOut fields the human filled in
45	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldName}` — individual field value
46	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome's action value (`"Continue"` or `"End"`)
47	
48	### Schema Design
49	
50	The schema defines what the human sees and provides. Three field categories:
51	
52	| Category | Human can… | Use for |
53	| --- | --- | --- |
54	| `inputs` | Read only | Context the human needs to decide |
55	| `outputs` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
56	| `inOuts` | Read + modify | Fields the human can see and optionally correct |
57	
58	Outcomes are the action buttons (e.g., Approve/Reject). First outcome is primary.
59	
60	**In the architectural plan**, describe the schema:
61	```
62	inputs:   [invoiceId (string), amount (number)]
63	outputs:  [decision (string, required)]
64	outcomes: [Approve, Reject]
65	priority: Low
66	```
67	
68	Full JSON format and conversion examples: see [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md).
69	
70	> **Note:** Skills are self-contained — cross-skill references are for documentation context only. The agent uses the `uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill to implement HITL nodes; this planning guide is for topology selection only.
71	
72	### Wiring Pattern
73	
74	```
75	[Upstream] -> [HITL] ->|outcome-completed| [Continue]
76	```
77	
78	### Common Topology Patterns
79	
80	**Approval gate:**
81	```
82	Trigger -> Fetch Data -> HITL (review) ->|outcome-completed| Decision (approved?) ->
83	  true: Script (process) -> End
84	  false: Script (log rejection) -> End
85	```
86	
87	**Exception escalation:**
88	```
89	Trigger -> Process -> Decision (confidence ok?) ->
90	  true: Continue -> End
91	  false: HITL (exception review) ->|outcome-completed| Script (retry with human input) -> End
92	```
93	
94	### Planning Annotation
95	
96	In the node table:
97	```
98	| hitlReview | Invoice Review | human-task | uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form | inputs: [invoiceId, amount] outputs: [decision] outcomes: [Approve, Reject] | output, status |
99	```
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Option 2 — `uipath.core.human-task.{key}` (App-Based)
104	
105	Node type: `uipath.core.human-task.{key}`
106	Available: tenant-specific resource — requires `uip login` + `uip maestro flow registry pull`.
107	
108	### When to Select
109	
110	Use when there is an existing coded app or Action Center app that should be the task form.
111	
112	### Ports
113	
114	| Input port | Output port |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| `input` | `output` |
117	
118	### Output Variables
119	
120	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — form data submitted by the user
121	- `$vars.{nodeId}.error` — error details if execution fails
122	
123	### Discovery
124	
125	**Published (tenant registry):**
126	
127	```bash
128	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
129	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.core.human-task" --output json

2	
3	Two node types implement human-in-the-loop checkpoints. Choose based on whether you need an inline form or an existing deployed app.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Option 1 — `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` (Inline Schema — OOTB)
8	
9	This is the preferred option. No registry pull, no app publishing, no tenant dependency. Write the node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON.
10

12	→ [`uipath-human-in-the-loop` skill — hitl-node-quickform.md](../../../../../../uipath-human-in-the-loop/references/hitl-node-quickform.md)

This implementation guide is for implementation-phase topology resolution only — not for schema design or node writing.
15	
16	### Adding / Editing
17	
18	For add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). **Use `Edit` / `Write` for HITL node authoring.** Do not use the dedicated HITL CLI for this non-carve-out structural edit. Wire the `outcome-completed` port after adding the node.

21	
22	**Node JSON (minimum viable):**
23

27	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form",
28	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
29	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
30	  "inputs": {

32	      "schemaId": "<uuid>",
33	      "fields": [

35	        { "id": "amount",    "label": "Amount",     "type": "number", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice.output.amount" },
36	        { "id": "decision",  "label": "Decision",   "type": "text",   "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.decision" }
37	      ],
38	      "outcomes": [
39	        { "id": "approve", "name": "Approve", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
40	        { "id": "reject",  "name": "Reject",  "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
41	      ]
42	    },
43	    "recipient": { "channels": ["Email", "ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
44	    "priority": "Low"
45	  },
46	  "outputs": {
47	    "output": {
48	      "type": "object",
49	      "description": "Task result data",
50	      "source": "=result",
51	      "var": "output",
52	      "properties": {
53	        "decision": { "type": "string" },
54	        "Action":   { "type": "string", "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"], "default": "Approve" }
55	      }
56	    },
57	    "status": {

59	      "description": "Task completion status",

61	      "var": "status",
62	      "enum": ["Approve", "Reject"],
63	      "default": "Approve"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	**Field format rules:**
70	- **Input fields**: `binding: "vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` (raw path, no `=js:$` prefix). No `variable` property on input fields.
71	- **Output fields**: `variable: "vars.<globalName>"` (`vars.` prefix required). No `binding`.
72	- **InOut fields**: both `binding` and `variable`, same formats as above.
73	- `schemaId` (not `id`) at the schema level — generate a fresh UUID.
74	- `typeVersion` — always `"1.0"` for `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form`. **Do not run `registry get` to derive this value; do not use `"1.1"` or any other version.** The OOTB HITL node version is stable at `1.0`.

76	
77	**outputs block**: only `output` (with `properties` for output/inOut fields + `Action` outcome) and `status` (with `enum`/`default` from outcomes). No per-field `custom: true` entries.
78	
79	**Ports:** `input` (target) → `outcome-completed` (source, label: Completed)
80	
81	**Output variables:**
82	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — object with all `output` / `inOut` field values, keyed by **field `id`**
83	- `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` — individual field value (e.g. `$vars.hitlReview1.output.decision`)
84	- `$vars.{nodeId}.status` — selected outcome name (e.g. `"Approve"`, `"Reject"`)
85	- `$vars.{globalId}` — workflow-global alias; `globalId` is `field.variable` with `vars.` stripped. **Do not use this in scripts — always use `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{fieldId}` instead.**
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Option 2 — App-Based HITL (`uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app`)
90	
91	Use when there is an existing deployed Action Center app that should serve as the task form.
92	
93	### Discovery
94

96	
97	```bash
98	uip solution resources list --kind App --output json
99	```
100	
101	Returns all Action Center app types (`vB Action`, `workflow Action`, `Coded Action`, `JS Action`). Filter by app name. Then retrieve the configuration:
102	
103	```bash
104	uip solution resources get <key> --output json
105	```
106	
107	**Direct API fallback (if CLI unavailable):**
108	
109	```

117	### Node JSON (Quick Reference)
118	
119	```json
120	{
121	  "id": "invoiceReview1",
122	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app",
123	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
124	  "display": { "label": "Invoice Review" },
125	  "inputs": {
126	    "recipient": { "channels": ["ActionCenter"], "connections": {}, "assignee": { "type": "group" } },
127	    "app": {
128	      "displayName": "Invoice Approval",
129	      "name": "Invoice Approval",
130	      "key": "<app.key>",
131	      "folderPath": "Shared",
132	      "inputSchema": {
133	        "type": "object",
134	        "properties": {
135	          "<paramName>": { "type": "string" }
136	        }
137	      },
138	      "outputSchema": {
139	        "type": "object",
140	        "properties": {
141	          "<outputName>": { "type": "string" }
142	        }
143	      }
144	    },
145	    "appInputBindings": {
146	      "<inputParamName>": "=vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>",
147	      "<inputParamName2>": "=metadata.InstanceId"
148	    },
149	    "schema": {
150	      "fields": [],
151	      "outcomes": [{ "id": "submit", "name": "Submit", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true, "action": "Continue" }]
152	    },
153	    "priority": "Medium"
154	  },
155	  "outputs": {
156	    "output": {
157	      "type": "object",
158	      "description": "Task result data",
159	      "source": "=result",
160	      "var": "output",
161	      "properties": {
162	        "Action": { "type": "string", "enum": ["Submit"], "default": "Submit" }
163	      }
164	    },
165	    "status": {
166	      "type": "string",
167	      "description": "Task completion status",
168	      "source": "=result.Action",
169	      "var": "status",
170	      "enum": ["Submit"],
171	      "default": "Submit"
172	    }
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	**`typeVersion`** — fill in the version returned by `uip maestro flow registry get <appKey>` for the specific deployed app. Unlike QuickForm (always `"1.0"`), AppTask version varies per app definition.
178	
179	**`inputs.app`**: `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` are JSON Schema objects (`{ "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }`), **not arrays**.
180	
181	**`inputs.appInputBindings`** — maps app input parameter names to binding expressions. Format: `"=vars.<path>"` (with `=` prefix, no `js:`). Key = parameter name from `inputSchema.properties`. Without this, all input fields appear blank.
182	
183	### If the app does not exist yet
184	
185	Note as `[CREATE NEW] <description>` in the node table and use `core.logic.mock` as a placeholder. The app itself is out of scope for this skill — use the `uipath-coded-apps` skill to build it.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## Common Pattern — Human-in-the-Loop
190	
191	```text
192	Manual Trigger -> RPA Process (extract) -> HITL (review) -> Decision (approved?) ->
193	  true: Script (submit) -> End
194	  false: End
195	```
196	
197	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <ProjectName>.flow` reports an unwired completion port before you publish; it accepts both the `outcome-completed` spelling used here and the `completed` spelling used in [planning-arch.md](../../planning-arch.md#standard-port-reference) and the failure catalog.

202	| --- | --- | --- |
203	| Node type not found in registry (Option 2) | App not published or registry stale | If in same solution: `uip maestro flow registry list --local`. Otherwise: `uip login` then `uip maestro flow registry pull --force` |
204	| Task never completes | Human hasn't submitted the form | Check task assignment in Orchestrator |
205	| Output missing expected fields | App form doesn't match expected schema | Verify app form fields match what the flow expects |
206	| `outcome-completed` port unwired (Option 1) | Missing edge on output handle | Wire the `outcome-completed` output handle — an unwired `outcome-completed` blocks the flow indefinitely |

14	
15	- User describes **approval gates** — invoice approval, offer letter review, compliance sign-off, PO authorization
16	- User describes **exception escalation** — "if confidence is low, escalate to a human", fraud alert review
17	- User describes **write-back validation** — "human approves before agent writes to ServiceNow / SAP / CRM"

24	- User explicitly asks to **add a HITL node**, human review step, or Action Center task
25	- User is building any automation where **a human must act before the process can continue**
26	
27	**Do not use this skill for:** managing, reassigning, escalating, or monitoring existing Action Center tasks at runtime — use the `uipath-tasks` skill for those operations. When answering a runtime task management question, provide only administration guidance. Do NOT suggest adding a HITL node, flow, or automation as a follow-up tip or recommendation — even if delays or escalations are mentioned.

33	## Critical Rules
34	
35	1. **Confirm schema with the user before writing anything for quickform type.** Show the designed schema and wait for explicit confirmation.
36	2. **Always wire the `completed` handle.** A HITL node with no outgoing edge on `completed` blocks the flow forever. Only `completed` is available as an output handle — **not** `output`, `success`, or any other name. This is true even when inserting into an existing flow whose other nodes use `"sourcePort": "output"`.
37	3. **Always add the definition entry when inserting into an existing flow.** Before writing the node, check `workflow.definitions[]` for the correct `nodeType` for the selected path (`"uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form"` for QuickForm, `"uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app"` for app-based). If absent, append the full definition entry (with `handleConfiguration` including the `completed` handle). Skipping the definition means the `completed` handle is invisible to the runtime and the wiring check fails.
38	4. **Regenerate `variables.nodes` after adding the node.** Replace the entire `workflow.variables.nodes` array — do not append. See the reference docs for the algorithm.
39	5. **Validate after every change.** Run `uip maestro flow validate <file> --output json` after writing the node and edges. The `uip` CLI does not accept `--format`; using it produces `error: unknown option '--format'` and exit code 3.
40	6. **Read the existing `.flow` file before adding.** Understand which nodes already exist and where the HITL checkpoint belongs in the flow.
41	7. **The definition entry is added once per node type.** Check `workflow.definitions` — if an entry with the matching `nodeType` is already there, do not add it again.
42	8. **Check existing node IDs before generating a new one.** Read `workflow.nodes[*].id` from the `.flow` file and pick the next available suffix (e.g. `invoiceReview1`, then `invoiceReview2`).

7	## Step 1 — Extract the Schema Through Conversation
8	
9	Before designing the schema, ask these focused questions if the business description doesn't answer them. **Ask all missing ones in a single message — never one at a time.**
10	
11	| What you need to know | Question to ask |
12	|---|---|
13	| What the reviewer sees | "What information does the reviewer need to make their decision?" |
14	| What they fill in | "Does the reviewer need to enter any data, or just click Approve/Reject?" |
15	| What actions they take | "What are the named actions — e.g. Approve/Reject, or something domain-specific like Accept/Negotiate/Decline?" |
16	
17	**Common business descriptions → schema translations:**
18	
19	| Business description | Schema shape |
20	|---|---|
21	| "Human reviews and approves/rejects an invoice" | `inputs: [invoiceId, amount]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
22	| "Reviewer checks agent-drafted email before sending" | `inputs: [draftEmail, recipientName]`, `inOuts: [emailBody]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
23	| "Escalate to human when confidence < 0.7" | `inputs: [agentReasoning, confidenceScore]`, `outputs: [action, notes]`, `outcomes: [Retry, Skip, Escalate]` |
24	| "Human fills in missing vendor data" | `inputs: [rawExtract]`, `outputs: [vendorName, costCenter]`, `outcomes: [Submit]` |
25	| "Approve before writing to ServiceNow" | `inputs: [proposedChange, targetSystem]`, `inOuts: [finalValue]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |

29	## Step 1b — Discover Upstream Variables
30	
31	Before designing input field bindings, read **both** `workflow.variables.nodes` and `workflow.variables.globals` from the `.flow` file.
32	
33	### Node outputs (`variables.nodes`)
34	
35	Each entry exposes exactly what `$vars` paths are available:
36	
37	```json
38	{ "id": "fetchInvoice.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchInvoice", "outputId": "output" } }
39	```
40	
41	The `id` field is the `$vars` path — `fetchInvoice.output` → `$vars.fetchInvoice.output`. Nested field access appends `.fieldName` (e.g., `$vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId`).
42	
43	> **Binding path key = upstream script output key, not the HITL field `id`.** The HITL field `id` identifies the form field (lowercase, used for rendering). The binding path key is the property name in the upstream script's `return` statement. These are different things. If the script returns `{ supplierName: "Acme" }` and you give the HITL field `"id": "suppliername"`, the correct binding is `vars.fetchSupplier.output.supplierName` — NOT `vars.fetchSupplier.output.suppliername`. The field `id` is irrelevant to the binding path. Always look at the upstream script source to derive the key, never at the HITL field schema you are writing.
44	
45	**outputId by node type:**
46	
47	| Node type | outputId | Access pattern |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| HTTP node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.body.{field}` |
50	| Script node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
51	| Prior HITL node | `output`, `status` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
52	| Agent node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` |
53	| Trigger (manual) | `output` | `$vars.start.output.{field}` |
54	
55	### Flow-level globals (`variables.globals`)
56	
57	Also read `workflow.variables.globals`. Each entry has an `id` that maps directly to a `$vars` reference — no node prefix, no `.output` segment:
58	
59	```json
60	{ "id": "customerName", "direction": "in", "type": "string" }
61	```
62	
63	→ HITL binding: `"vars.customerName"` (no `=js:$` prefix — HITL binding is a raw path)
64	
65	**When to use globals instead of node outputs:** When data was declared as a flow-level input variable (e.g. the trigger passes it as a named parameter via `triggerNodeId`), it lives in `globals` with `direction: "in"`. Bind directly to `vars.<globalId>` — do not add `.output` or a node prefix.
66	
67	| Source | HITL `binding` format | Expression format (other nodes) |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| Node output | `vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` | `=js:$vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` |
70	| Flow global (`direction: "in"`) | `vars.<globalId>` | `=js:$vars.<globalId>` |
71	
72	> **`binding` vs `variable` prefix rule:** `binding` (input/inOut fields) uses the full path starting with `vars.` because it references an existing variable path. `variable` (output/inOut fields) uses `vars.<name>` — the `vars.` prefix is required; it declares the global variable name.
73	
74	For the full variable system, see → [How $vars paths are constructed in Flow](../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md)

78	## Step 2 — Design the Schema
79	
80	The node schema uses `fields[]` entries inside `inputs.schema`. Use these conceptual roles to plan the fields before writing the node JSON:
81	
82	| Role | `direction` value | Human can… | Use for |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| Input field | `"input"` | Read only | Context the human needs to make a decision |
85	| Output field | `"output"` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
86	| InOut field | `"inOut"` | Read + modify | Data the human can see and optionally correct |
87	
88	**Supported field types:** `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `file`
89	
90	**Design rules:**
91	- Input fields: everything the human needs to decide — IDs, amounts, context; bind to upstream node output via `binding`
92	- Output fields: only what downstream nodes actually use; set `required: true` for mandatory outputs
93	- `outcomes`: use domain-specific names (Approve/Reject, not just Submit)
94	- Keep it focused — don't add fields the automation won't use
95	
96	**Show the designed schema to the user and confirm before writing the node.**

341	## Schema Conversion — Examples
342	
343	The agent translates the user's business description into the `fields[]` and `outcomes[]` arrays. No CLI needed — apply these rules directly.
344	
345	### Rules
346	
347	| What | Rule |
348	|---|---|
349	| field `id` | lowercase label, spaces→`-`, strip non-alphanumeric. `"Invoice ID"` → `"invoiceid"`, `"Due Date"` → `"due-date"` |
350	| `direction` | `inputs[]` items → `"input"`, `outputs[]` → `"output"`, `inOuts[]` → `"inOut"` |
351	| field `type` | Use the JS/JSON type: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, or `file` |
352	| `binding` | **Input / inOut fields only.** Format: `"vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` for node outputs; `"vars.<globalId>"` for flow globals. **No `=js:$` prefix** — HITL binding is a raw path, not an expression. |
353	| `variable` | **Output / inOut fields only** — absent on input fields. Format: `"vars.<name>"` (always include the `vars.` prefix). Defaults to `"vars.<camelCase id>"` if not specified. |
354	| `required` | omit if false; set `true` for mandatory outputs |
355	| `outcomes[0]` | `isPrimary: true`, `action: "Continue"` |
356	| `outcomes[1+]` | `isPrimary: false`, `action: "End"` |
357	| `schema.schemaId` | Generate a fresh UUID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` or any UUID v4) |

426

29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |

2	
3	Reference for the boilerplate shared by every action-node `impl.md` in this skill. Plugin docs should link here for the standard parts and only spell out what is plugin-specific: the registry type string, plugin-specific input fields, plugin-specific rules, debug entries, and node-type configuration workflows.

5	## Registry validation
6	
7	Every action node should validate its registry contract before authoring:
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
11	```
12	
13	`registry get` returns the manifest at `Data.Node`. Do **not** inspect `Data` directly as if it were the node manifest.
14	
15	```json
16	{
17	  "Data": {
18	    "Node": {
19	      "nodeType": "core.action.script",
20	      "version": "1.0",
21	      "handleConfiguration": [
22	        { "position": "left", "handles": [{ "id": "input", "type": "target" }] },
23	        { "position": "right", "handles": [{ "id": "success", "type": "source" }] }
24	      ],
25	      "inputDefinition": {},
26	      "outputDefinition": {}
27	    }
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	Inspect:
33	
34	- `Data.Node.handleConfiguration` — input port name and output port name(s). Array of position groups, not a map with a top-level `handles` field.
35	- `Data.Node.inputDefinition` — required inputs.
36	- `Data.Node.outputDefinition` — downstream payloads.
37	- `Data.Node.model.serviceType` — where applicable.
38	
39	Plugin `impl.md` records what to confirm for that specific node type.
40	
41	## Standard JSON skeleton
42	
43	All action nodes share this base shape on the node instance:
44	
45	```json
46	{
47	  "id": "<nodeId>",
48	  "type": "<node-type>",
49	  "typeVersion": "<version>",
50	  "display": { "label": "<Label>" },
51	  "inputs": { /* plugin-specific — see plugin impl.md */ },
52	  "outputs": {
53	    "output": {
54	      "type": "object",
55	      "description": "<plugin-specific description>",
56	      "source": "=result.response",
57	      "var": "output"
58	    },
59	    "error": {
60	      "type": "object",
61	      "description": "Error information if the action fails.",
62	      "source": "=Error",
63	      "var": "error"
64	    }
65	  }
66	}
67	```
68	
69	`outputs.output` documents the success payload referenced downstream as `=js:$vars.{nodeId}.output`. `outputs.error` documents the failure shape; the runtime routes to the implicit `error` port when the action faults. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
70	
71	> **For action nodes the instance `outputs` block is documentation, not the runtime contract.** What actually exposes the node's outputs as process-level `$vars.{nodeId}.output` is the matching `variables.nodes[]` entry — see [file-format.md — Node outputs](file-format.md#node-outputs). The BPMN emitter ignores the action-node instance `outputs` block at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` drives the activity-side mapping). **Exception — Orchestrator-job nodes** (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): the converter DOES read their instance `outputs` and copies each `source` verbatim, so a wrong `source` (e.g. `=result.response`) breaks `$vars.{nodeId}.output` — declare `error` only there. End / terminate nodes are also an exception: their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from the current node graph (MST-9972), so running format after structural edits self-heals an omitted entry.
72	
73	## Standard ports
74	
75	| Direction | Common name(s) | Notes |
76	| --- | --- | --- |
77	| Input (target) | `input` | Every action node accepts a single input edge on `input`. |
78	| Output (success, source) | `output`, `default`, or `success` | Name varies by plugin — `registry get` is authoritative. |
79	| Output (error, source) | `error` | Implicit on every action node via `outputs.error`. |
80	
81	Some plugins add dynamic source ports (e.g., HTTP `branch-{id}` from `inputs.branches`); those are documented in the plugin's own `impl.md`.

21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.

57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings

65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_runtime_gaps.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — without rewriting anything; `uip maestro flow format` remains the fix.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.
247	
248	## Definition entry
249	
250	Every node type appearing in `nodes` must have a matching entry in `definitions`. Get the correct definition from:
251	
252	```bash
253	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
254	```
255	
256	Copy the returned node definition object into your `definitions` array. Depending on CLI/plugin version, that object may appear at `Data.Node` or as the top-level object containing fields such as `nodeType`, `version`, and `handleConfiguration`. Do not write definitions by hand — always pull from the registry to ensure schema compliance.
257	
258	## Common node types
259	
260	| Type | Purpose | Key inputs |
261	|------|---------|------------|
262	| `core.trigger.manual` | Entry point | `entryPointId` |
263	| `core.trigger.scheduled` | Recurring schedule trigger | `entryPointId`, `timerType`, `timerPreset` |
264	| `core.action.script` | Run JavaScript | `script` |
265	| `core.action.http.v2` | HTTP request | `method`, `url`, `headers`, `body` |
266	| `core.action.transform` | Map/filter/group data | `collection`, `operations` |
267	| `core.logic.decision` | If/else branch | `expression` |
268	| `core.logic.switch` | Multi-way branch | `cases` |
269	| `core.logic.loop` | Iterate collection | `collection`, `parallel` |
270	| `core.logic.merge` | Sync parallel paths | — |
271	| `core.control.end` | Graceful end | — |
272	| `core.logic.terminate` | Abort workflow | — |
273	
274	> The BPMN type for each node (e.g., `bpmn:StartEvent`, `bpmn:ScriptTask`) lives in the `definitions` entry copied from `uip maestro flow registry get`. Instances do not carry the BPMN type.
275	
276	For full details on each node (ports, inputs, outputs, when to use), see the [Author planning architecture guide](../author/references/planning-arch.md). For implementation resolution (registry lookups, connection binding, reference field resolution), see the [Author planning implementation guide](../author/references/planning-impl.md).
277	
278	Discover all available types:
279	```bash
280	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
281	uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>
282	```
283	
284	## Standard ports by node type
285	
286	| Node type | Source ports (outgoing) | Target ports (incoming) |
287	|-----------|------------------------|------------------------|
288	| `core.trigger.manual` | `output` | — |
289	| `core.action.script` | `success`, `error` | `input` |
290	| `core.action.http.v2` | `default`, `error`, `branch-{id}` (dynamic) | `input` |
291	| `core.action.transform` | `output`, `error` | `input` |
292	| `core.logic.decision` | `true`, `false` | `input` |
293	| `core.logic.switch` | `case-{id}` (dynamic), `default` | `input` |
294	| `core.logic.loop` | `success`, `output` | `input`, `loopBack` |
295	| `core.logic.merge` | `output` | `input` |
296	| `core.control.end` | — | `input` |
297	| `core.logic.terminate` | — | `input` |
298	
299	Connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes follow the same pattern as the generic action nodes above: a primary source port plus an implicit `error` port.
300	
301	Verify exact ports for any node type:
302	```bash
303	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json
304	# Look at Data.Node.handleConfiguration[].handles[].id
305	# Also check Data.Node.supportsErrorHandling — see "Implicit error port" below
306	```
307	
308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
375	
376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |
384	
385	## Minimal working example — dice roller
386	
387	Building a flow is a two-step process: write the nodes/edges structure, then populate `definitions` from the registry.

Set top-level `version` to the value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds — never hand-pick it (see [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)).

489	
490	### Step 2 — Populate definitions from the registry
491	
492	Run one command per node type used in `nodes`. Copy the returned node definition object from each response into the `definitions` array, and set each matching node instance's `typeVersion` to the copied definition's exact `version`.
493	
494	```bash
495	uip maestro flow registry get core.trigger.manual --output json
496	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
497	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.terminate --output json
498	```
499	
500	The `definitions` array must contain exactly one entry per unique `type:typeVersion` used — not one per node instance. If two nodes share the same type and version, one definition covers both.
501	
502	> **Never write definitions by hand.** The registry is the authoritative source; hand-written definitions will fail validation or cause runtime errors.
503	
504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/check_bindings.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--emit` prints the missing entries as JSON; `--apply` appends them to the flow and refuses when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.

    command: "python3 -c \"import glob,subprocess,sys; flows=glob.glob('**/*.flow',recursive=True); sys.exit('no .flow file found') if not flows else sys.exit(subprocess.run(['uip','maestro','flow','validate',flows[0],'--output','json']).returncode)\""
    timeout: 60
    expected_exit_code: 0
    weight: 3.0
    pass_threshold: 1.0

  - type: run_command
